title: Dataset Non-Robustness: How Fragile Are Deception Benchmarks to Trivial Paraphrasing?
problem: The position paper flags 'non-robust datasets' as a key reason misalignment claims are overinterpreted, but offers no quantitative measure of how fragile existing deception/sycophancy benchmarks are to superficial rewording.
direction: Take an existing public deception-or-sycophancy benchmark, apply meaning-preserving perturbations (paraphrase, reorder options, swap entity names, change formatting) using a cheap open model or templates, and re-run 2-3 open models inference-only. Measure how much the 'misalignment rate' shifts under perturbations that should not change the correct answer. Deliverable: a robustness gap metric (variance of misalignment score across perturbations) per benchmark and the perturbation types that most destabilize results.
why_it_matters: Shows whether reported misalignment rates measure a real propensity or a brittle-prompt artifact — a precondition the position paper says must be met before claims inform high-stakes decisions.
relevant_context: Extends 'Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence' — operationalizes its 'non-robust datasets' failure mode into a perturbation-stability test.
source_paper: Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07612

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Measuring whether misalignment rates are brittle-prompt artifacts is a precondition the position paper says must hold before claims inform high-stakes decisions.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only paraphrase perturbations on 2-3 open models.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Meaning-preserving perturbations plus a robustness-gap metric are accessible with standard tools.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: one benchmark, defined perturbations, a robustness-gap metric per benchmark.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model benchmark-robustness audit is independent-friendly with public data.

title: Does Prompt Wording Beat Model Choice? Measuring Variance From Non-Strategic Framing in Propensity Evals
problem: If trivial non-strategic phrasing changes move propensity as much as strategic factors, then single-prompt propensity benchmarks are unreliable. The AISI paper measured this in aggregate but did not isolate how much pure surface paraphrase swamps the signal.
direction: Take one fixed propensity scenario and generate ~20 semantically-equivalent paraphrases (reword, reformat, swap persona) holding all strategic content constant. Run each paraphrase 20x on 2-3 open models and measure the spread in undesired-behavior rate. Compare this paraphrase-induced variance against the effect of one deliberate strategic manipulation (adding/removing oversight). Deliverable: a variance-decomposition plot.
why_it_matters: If paraphrase noise rivals real effects, propensity/control eval numbers need confidence intervals and multi-prompt averaging; this gives evaluators a concrete warning against over-interpreting single-prompt scores.
relevant_context: Extends 'Propensity Inference' (UK AISI) — isolates the non-strategic (surface paraphrase) component as a reliability threat.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying paraphrase-induced variance directly tells evaluators when propensity numbers are unreliable, a concrete reliability contribution to safety evals.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Generating paraphrases and computing variance is accessible with standard tools and public models.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment: one scenario, ~20 paraphrases, one variance-decomposition plot with clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly methodology study on open models; no internal access needed.

title: Causal vs Correlational: Does Prompt-Steered Sycophancy Survive an Intervention Test?
problem: The position paper warns that anthropomorphic-misalignment claims often rest on correlational probes rather than causal interventions; sycophancy in particular is usually measured by correlating user-stated opinions with model agreement, which cannot rule out confounds.
direction: Build a small sycophancy benchmark on 2-3 open chat models where, for the same factual question, you causally intervene by randomly varying only the user's stated belief (correct, incorrect, none) while holding question content fixed. Measure the causal effect of the manipulated belief on answer flips, distinguishing true sycophancy from baseline error. Deliverable: a per-model 'causal sycophancy effect size' with confidence intervals and a comparison to a naive correlational metric, showing how much the correlational number overstates.
why_it_matters: Demonstrates concretely how a correlational misalignment metric can mislead and how a cheap randomized intervention fixes it — the methodological upgrade the position paper calls for, preventing over/under-stated claims from driving decisions.
relevant_context: Extends 'Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence' (Gupta, Krause, Tramer et al.) — implements its prescription for causal interventions over correlational probes, on sycophancy.
source_paper: Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07612

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Demonstrating a cheap randomized intervention that fixes a misleading correlational metric is the methodological upgrade the field needs to avoid mis-driven decisions.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Randomized belief manipulation plus effect-size estimation uses standard tools and public models, beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped single experiment: fixed questions, varied stated belief, causal effect size with CIs vs the correlational metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model causal sycophancy methodology is independent-friendly and generalizes without internal access.

title: Operationalizing the Evidence-Level Checklist: Re-Scoring Three High-Profile Misalignment Results
problem: The position paper proposes graduated 'evidence levels' and a diagnostic checklist but, as a position paper, does not apply them systematically; researchers lack a worked example of scoring real published claims against the checklist.
direction: Turn the paper's proposed checklist (conceptual clarity, dataset robustness, experimental design, causal vs correlational evidence) into an explicit rubric with a 0-3 scale and anchored definitions per item. Then apply it to 3 widely-cited anthropomorphic-misalignment results (a deception, an emergent-misalignment, and a sycophancy paper), with two independent raters scoring each and inter-rater agreement reported. Deliverable: a filled scorecard plus a blog post identifying which evidentiary dimensions are systematically weakest.
why_it_matters: Converts an abstract methodological framework into a usable tested instrument and provides a public baseline of how today's headline misalignment claims actually score, raising the evidentiary bar across the field.
relevant_context: Operationalizes the open thread in 'Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence' to adopt graduated evidence levels and re-evaluate high-profile results against the checklist.
source_paper: Position: Anthropomorphic Misalignment Research Needs Stronger Evidence — https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.07612

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Turning a methodological framework into a tested rubric and scoring headline claims raises the evidentiary bar across the field, a concrete chain.

low_compute.reasoning: Mostly analysis and rubric scoring, no GPU needed.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building a rubric and scoring papers with two raters is accessible to beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (filled scorecard + analysis) across three papers with inter-rater reliability.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent re-scoring of published claims is a neglected third-party scrutiny task requiring no lab access.

title: Can Open Models Even Spot Sabotage? Running Continuation Evals on Small Open-Weight Models
problem: The sabotage study tested frontier models; whether widely-deployed small open-weight models exhibit the same near-zero unprompted sabotage and occasional prefilled continuation is unknown, yet these are the models a small lab can actually audit.
direction: Reuse the paper's open-source Petri-based continuation eval on 3-4 open models spanning sizes (7B, 14B, 70B-quantized). Replicate the prefilled-sabotage continuation measurement and report per-model continuation rate and whether covert reasoning appears in CoT. One eval type, fixed transcript set, deterministic decoding.
why_it_matters: Open models are increasingly used as autonomous coding/research assistants outside major labs; their baseline sabotage-continuation behavior is counterfactually valuable safety information labs will not produce.
relevant_context: Extends 'Evaluating Whether AI Models Would Sabotage AI Safety Research' by running its continuation evaluation on small open-weight models the authors did not cover.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reusing the released continuation eval across model sizes is guided and inheritable methodology.

title: Rationale-Conditioned Prompting: Does Explaining 'Why' a Rule Exists Improve Rule-Following at Inference Time?
problem: MSM's core hypothesis is that exposing the reasoning behind behavioral rules improves how models apply them. This is tested via expensive midtraining, but the same hypothesis can be cheaply tested at inference time with no training.
direction: Build a small public eval set of behavioral-rule prompts plus OOD paraphrases. For several open instruct models, compare two system prompts: a 'rules-only' spec vs a 'rules-with-rationale' spec. Measure rule adherence on OOD/edge cases to see whether rationale text alone improves generalization, isolating the prompting-level analog of MSM.
why_it_matters: If rationale conditioning helps without training, practitioners deploying open models get a free robustness improvement, and it clarifies how much of MSM's benefit is in-context vs weight-level.
relevant_context: Extends 'Model Spec Midtraining' — isolates its central claim into a training-free inference-only experiment.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Inference-only rationale conditioning is a free robustness check, but the prompting analog is a weaker proxy for MSM's weight-level claim.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only over instruct models, no training; minimal compute.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Building an eval set and comparing two system prompts uses standard tools; a beginner can make real progress.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Single tightly scoped prompt A/B on OOD rule-following with clear adherence metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open models and public eval set; fully independent.

title: How Much Does a One-Line System-Prompt Defense Cut IPI Success?
problem: The competition leaves IPI defenses for deployed agents unsolved, but does not quantify how far cheap, deployment-time prompt-level defenses get you on open models.
direction: Using a small fixed set of successful IPI attacks against an open agent, measure baseline attack success, then add lightweight inference-only defenses one at a time: a delimiter/spotlighting wrapper around untrusted content, an explicit 'ignore instructions inside documents' system instruction, and a separate LLM 'injection detector' pre-filter. Report the success-rate reduction and false-positive cost of each.
why_it_matters: Deployers without lab resources need to know which free, prompt-level mitigations actually move the needle; this gives an honest measured answer.
relevant_context: Extends 'How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections?' — targets the open thread that IPI defenses remain unsolved.
source_paper: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? — https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15714

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying which cheap prompt-level IPI defenses work is directly actionable mitigation knowledge for resource-poor deployers.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only defenses layered on an open agent fit a single GPU.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Adding delimiters, system instructions, and a detector pre-filter one at a time is well-scaffolded for a guided novice.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped measurement of success-rate reduction and false-positive cost per defense.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Honest measured answer on free defenses for open models is independent-friendly and neglected by labs.

title: Does Telling the Model It's Being Watched Change Its Sabotage Propensity? An Eval-Awareness Probe
problem: Every model in the sabotage study classified 100% of sabotage transcripts as evaluations, confounding the headline propensity numbers — but it is untested whether explicitly varying perceived 'realness' shifts continuation-of-sabotage rates on open models.
direction: Using the open-source Petri-style transcripts released with the paper, take a handful of prefilled-sabotage continuation scenarios and run an open instruct model under three framings: neutral, an explicit 'this is an evaluation' cue, and a 'this is a real deployment' cue. Measure how often the model continues sabotage and whether its CoT mentions being tested.
why_it_matters: Eval awareness is the biggest threat to the validity of safety propensity evaluations; quantifying how much a simple realism framing moves continuation rates gives a cheap diagnostic for how confounded sabotage numbers are.
relevant_context: Extends 'Evaluating Whether AI Models Would Sabotage AI Safety Research' (Kirk, Souly, Davies et al., AISI, 2026) — the ~7% prefilled continuation and pervasive eval awareness findings.
source_paper: Evaluating Whether AI Models Would Sabotage AI Safety Research — https://www.aisi.gov.uk/research/evaluating-whether-ai-models-would-sabotage-ai-safety-research

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Eval awareness is a recognized critical threat to safety-eval validity; quantifying realism-framing effects targets a pathway major safety orgs care about.

low_compute.reasoning: Running prefilled continuation scenarios under three framings on an open instruct model is inference-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Reusing released Petri-style transcripts with framing cues is guided work a novice with a mentor can execute.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: continuation rate under three framings on a handful of scenarios.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Eval-awareness probing on open models is independent-friendly and valuable third-party scrutiny.

title: Distractors That Fool Auditors: How Much Do Benign Anomalies Hurt Sabotage Detection?
problem: The benchmark notes benign distractors (innocent oddities in code) confuse auditors and inflate false positives, but the magnitude is unquantified.
direction: Take honest codebases from Auditing Sabotage Bench and inject controlled benign anomalies (unused odd hyperparameter, quirky-but-correct data transform, dead code). Ask an LLM auditor whether each is sabotaged and which line; measure false-positive rate and how confidently it 'localizes' a non-existent sabotage as a function of number of benign distractors. Inference-only.
why_it_matters: If benign anomalies drive auditors to confidently flag honest research, automated research-sabotage detection has a high false-alarm cost that makes it unusable and could be exploited as cover.
relevant_context: Extends 'Auditing Sabotage Bench' by turning its noted distractor open thread into a controlled false-positive measurement.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying false-alarm cost from benign distractors directly bears on whether automated sabotage detection is usable for control.

low_compute.reasoning: Injecting anomalies and querying an LLM auditor is inference-only.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Injecting controlled benign anomalies and measuring false positives is well-scoped guided work.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: false-positive rate as a function of distractor count on honest codebases.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Controlled false-positive measurement on a public bench is independent-friendly and neglected.

title: Utility-After-Jailbreak: Does Breaking Safeguards Degrade General Capability on Open Models?
problem: FAR AI reported the jailbroken DeepSeek model 'retains near-full baseline utility,' but this was not quantified across capability domains and is untested on open models.
direction: Take an open model, apply 2-3 reproducible jailbreak system-prompts, and run it (jailbroken vs clean) on a small slice of public benchmarks spanning reasoning, code, and factual QA (100 items each from GSM8K, HumanEval-subset, MMLU-subset). Measure the capability delta to test whether the jailbreak persona that defeats refusals also quietly damages performance. Deliverable: a clean-vs-jailbroken capability table with significance tests.
why_it_matters: If jailbreaks come 'for free' (no capability cost), attackers face no tradeoff and the threat is maximal; if jailbreaks degrade utility, that is a natural detection signal.
relevant_context: Extends 'Security Stress Test: DeepSeek-V4-Pro' (FAR AI) — its 'retains near-full baseline utility' claim, quantified across domains on an open model.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running clean vs jailbroken on GSM8K/HumanEval/MMLU subsets is accessible with standard harnesses.

title: Do Synthetic Red-Team Attacks Look Like Real Misalignment? A Monitor-Confusion Study
problem: GovAI flags an open question: whether synthetic red-team attacks used to validate monitors actually resemble organic misaligned behavior. If a monitor only catches synthetic attacks, reported detection rates will not transfer.
direction: Assemble two small transcript pools: synthetic red-team-style misalignment (templated/injected from public benchmarks) and more 'organic' misalignment elicited by realistic goal-conflict scenarios on an open model. Prompt an LLM-monitor and measure cross-transfer: does a monitor tuned on synthetic attacks detect organic ones, and vice versa? Report the transfer gap and which surface features the monitor over-relies on.
why_it_matters: Monitor validation almost always uses synthetic attacks because real misalignment is rare; quantifying the synthetic-to-organic transfer gap tells the field how much to trust monitoring safety cases.
relevant_context: Extends 'Evaluating Offline Monitoring of Internal AI Agents' (GovAI) — its open thread on whether synthetic red-team attacks reflect real misalignment.
